fact: The DHIS2 Climate & Health country profile says DHIS2 has been used as South Sudan's national health management information system since 2020, covering routine data on a range of health programs.
The profile says the FLLOW-M dashboard within the national DHIS2 integrates historical malaria surveillance data with climate indicators, and DHIS2 is also used for disease surveillance.

The UNDP brief says the mSupply eLMIS at the Gumbo Warehouse is interoperable with DHIS2 and that an eLMIS dashboard was developed and integrated into DHIS2; it is rolled out to 105 of 145 health facilities (72.4%).
The WHO/MoH maturity assessment says South Sudan has implemented DHIS 2 at both the national and sub-national/district levels.
The WHO/MoH maturity assessment records the completeness rate for routine reports at 62% and for indicator data at 57%.

UNESCO says DHIS2 is widely used by the Government of South Sudan for routine health information and has supported the Ministry of Health in collecting data across states, counties, payams and bomas since 2018.

The DHIS2 Community report says a 12-month pilot (March 2025 to February 2026) of an offline-first DHIS2 Tracker program lets Boma Health Workers record household visits, childhood illness and immunisation follow-up digitally, with Ministry of Health leadership.
